newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds strengthen in steady trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds strengthen in steady trade.

text.p: Irish bonds strengthened on Friday in light but consistent trade, with the market holding steady in the face of volatility elsewhere in Europe, dealers said.

"The market seems to be pretty much detached from the ups and downs seen this week by the UK and Scandinavian markets, for example," a dealer said. "Today in the 10-year bonds we're outperforming both the UK and Germany."
A rally in the U.S. market overnight had improved the market's mood following Thursday's stumble on speculation that U.S. interest rates were set to rise, dealers said.
Remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday about the need to act pre-emptively to fight inflation lashed markets already fretting over U.S. rates policy.

"Like everybody else we're waiting to see what comes out of Tuesday's FOMC meeting, but most bond markets are already pricing in a quarter point rise in U.S. interest rates," a dealer said. "We're expecting the Fed to tighten short rates by about 25 basis points."
Investors were responding reasonably well to the threat of higher interest rates and the effect on yield value, dealers said.
"The feeling is that a seven percent rate on the long bond is fairly attractive."
The market would benefit from Thursday's Irish CPI figures, dealers said, which appeared to remove any doubt over Ireland's ability to meet the Maastricht inflation criterion this year.

The Irish February consumer price index showed a lower-than-expected rise of 0.6 percent month-on-month, giving a year-on-year increase of 1.5 percent. Forecasts ranged from a rise of up to 1.0 percent m/m and 2.0 percent y/y.
By mid-afternoon Friday the spread on the Irish 10-year bond had narrowed to 98 basis points over Germany, dealers said.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 26 pence from Thursday's close at 101.11 to yield 6.20 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 35 pence from the close at 107.30 to yield 6.91 percent.
